text: CHAPTER 28
speaker: Narrator

text: The City Beneath the City
speaker: Narrator
note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

text: They did not return to the plaza, and the City did not force them to.
speaker: Narrator

text: Instead it simply rearranged the streets until every corridor they chose led back to the same narrow alcove. Zik noticed the first repetition when he saw the cracked tile under the covered walkway for the second time. Balag noticed it when the same dripping water resumed its patient count. Ninsun stopped writing after the third return and simply stared at the wall as though the stone itself had insulted her.
speaker: Narrator

text: The man who had refused still sat where they had left him, knees drawn up, humming under his breath. He did not look surprised to see them again.
speaker: Narrator

text: You tried the eastern passage,
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: he said. It was not a question.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Balag's axe rested across his shoulders.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: We are walking in circles.
speaker: Balag

text: No,
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: the man answered.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: You are being returned. Circles would be kinder.
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: Enhedu's knife was already in her hand.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: How many times does it do this?
speaker: Enhedu

text: The man smiled with half his mouth.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Until you stop trying to leave the way you came, or until you decide the price of staying is lower than the price of another attempt. Most people choose the second option before the fifth return.
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: Zik looked down the narrowing street they had just walked. The geometry had already begun to shift again; the far end no longer matched the memory of the last attempt. The mark under the linen on his palm pulsed once, slow and deliberate, as if confirming a ledger entry.
speaker: Narrator

text: They tried a fourth time anyway.
speaker: Narrator

text: This passage led behind the low wall of inventories and down a slope that grew colder with every step. The air tasted of iron and old paper. For several minutes the City allowed them the illusion of progress. Then the floor leveled, the walls widened, and the same alcove waited at the end of the corridor. The man was still humming.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag lowered the axe and sat on the paving stones without ceremony.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: I don't like this place.
speaker: Balag

text: That is sensible,
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: the man said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: I wasn't asking.
speaker: Balag

text: The living rarely do.
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: Ninsun had already moved to the long panel of wedge marks that ran along the wall opposite the alcove. She brushed dust from the deepest lines with careful fingers. The torchlight sank into the oily stone and did not return.
speaker: Narrator

text: These are older than the household inventories,
speaker: Ninsun

text: she said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Different hand. Different purpose.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Zik stepped closer. The mark on his palm had begun to warm in a way that no longer felt like warning. It felt like recognition.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun's stylus hovered above the first line.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: The root forms are familiar. Settlement. Binding. Debt. But the combinations refuse ordinary translation. The first line could mean discovered. Or summoned. Those are not the same thing.
speaker: Ninsun

text: No,
speaker: Zik

text: Zik said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: She continued, voice growing quieter.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: The people who sealed the upper city did not build what lies beneath it. The earliest records claim the first settlers entered from above and found roads, wells, storage chambers already waiting. They believed the place had been abandoned.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Balag looked at the man in the alcove.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: By whom?
speaker: Balag

text: Ninsun's finger stopped on a character whose edges had eroded.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: The word can mean inhabitants. It can also mean remains. Echoes. The dead.
speaker: Ninsun

text: The man gave a dry, unused laugh.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: I preferred it when we were only lost.
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: Enhedu's eyes stayed on him.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: You know this language.
speaker: Enhedu

text: I know what it cost.
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: Ninsun forced herself farther along the wall. The next section was more formal, the wedges deeper and more carefully arranged. Phrases repeated with bureaucratic insistence: the agreement, the binding, the debt below.
speaker: Narrator

text: Debt is not exact,
speaker: Ninsun

text: she said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Obligation. Price. Something owed to the foundation.
speaker: Ninsun
